formula.title: Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments: risk as a combination of likelihood and impact

bands.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained

bands.name: Very Low
bands.justification: Minimal exposure. Standard re-review every 2 years.

bands.name: Low
bands.justification: Acceptable with normal oversight. Annual re-review.

bands.name: Moderate
bands.justification: Original policy default: avoid. Change to 'Approved with Conditions' if your policy allows managed moderate risk.

bands.name: High
bands.justification: Avoid. Use only with formal leadership risk acceptance; re-review twice a year if accepted.

bands.name: Critical
bands.justification: Avoid. Use only with formal leadership risk acceptance.

factors.question: Does the vendor lack a recognized security framework or third-party certification (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001)?
factors.justification: An independent audit is the cheapest proof that baseline controls exist and are tested. Weighted 1 (not 2) because a certificate shows controls exist, not that they stop breaches.
factors.guidance: Check the vendor trust center. Ask for the SOC 2 Type II report (not just a logo).

references.title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into supplier relationships
Software Acquisition Guide for Government Enterprise Consumers

factors.question: Has the vendor had a data breach in the last three years?
factors.justification: Past breaches are the strongest single predictor available of future incidents, so this carries double weight.
factors.guidance: Search vendor name + breach/incident/disclosure. Note whether the incident was the vendor or its parent.

references.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into supplier relationships
Supplier risks are understood, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

factors.question: Has the vendor been in the news or in court for negative or questionable privacy practices in the last three years?
factors.justification: Regulatory actions and lawsuits show how a vendor treats data when no one is watching. Double weight, same as breaches.
factors.guidance: Search regulator sites (FTC, state AGs, EU DPAs) and major news. Cite the source.

references.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into supplier relationships
Supplier risks are understood, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

factors.question: Is the vendor small and early-stage (fewer than 200 staff AND in operation fewer than 5 years)?
factors.justification: Young, small vendors often lack a dedicated security team and are more likely to fold or be acquired. Single weight: size alone is not a flaw. NIST asks for supplier due diligence (GV.SC-06) but doesn't say small or young vendors are riskier. This weighting is an organization preference carried over from the original template.
factors.guidance: LinkedIn headcount and founding date are usually enough.

references.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into supplier relationships

factors.question: Does the vendor fail to disclose which AI model(s) power the product, who trained them, or what data was used?
factors.justification: If you cannot name the model you cannot assess where data goes or how outputs behave. Double weight for AI tools.
factors.guidance: Answer 'No' for non-AI software.

references.title: Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components, including third-party data or software
Value Chain and Component Integration

factors.question: Is this purchased outside of IT and Legal review (e.g., purchasing card, expensed, or free self-sign-up)?
factors.justification: Unmanaged purchases skip contract terms (DPA, liability, deletion) that limit damage when something goes wrong.
factors.guidance: Confirm with Procurement / the requesting team.

references.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are integrated into contracts
Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into supplier relationships

factors.question: What is the vendor's third-party security rating (e.g., UpGuard, Mozilla, Netskope CCI, SecurityScorecard, BitSight), on a 0-100 scale?
factors.justification: Independent outside-in rating. Bands carried over from the original template. 'Not rated' scores 2: unknown is treated as below average, not as worst case. NIST asks you to monitor supplier risk (GV.SC-07). Using an outside-in rating service is one way to do that; which service is your choice.
factors.guidance: Pick the band. Convert letter grades: A=76-100, B=51-75, C=26-50, D/F=0-25.

references.title: Supplier risks are understood, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

factors.question: Has the vendor been acquired, merged, or changed ownership in the last 12 months (or is one pending)?
factors.justification: Ownership changes often rewrite privacy terms, data-sharing and model choices after you have signed. The parent's record starts to apply.
factors.guidance: Check press releases and the vendor's 'about' page.

references.title: Supplier risks are understood, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

factors.factor: Sends data to other AI providers
factors.question: Does the product send our data to third-party AI / model providers (fourth parties)?
factors.justification: Each sub-processor is another place data can leak or be retained. Unknown scores the same as Yes.
factors.guidance: See the vendor's sub-processor list.

references.title: Policies and procedures address AI risks associated with third-party entities
Supplier risks are understood, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship

factors.question: Can the software take actions on its own (run code, send messages, change records, make purchases) without a person approving each one?
factors.justification: Agentic tools turn a bad output into a bad action. Double weight.
factors.guidance: Answer 'No' if every action needs human approval.

references.title: Excessive Agency
Human-AI Configuration

factors.question: Does the product lack single sign-on (SAML/OIDC) with enforceable MFA?
factors.justification: Without SSO, offboarding is manual and stolen passwords work.
factors.guidance: Check the plan tier being purchased; SSO is often enterprise-only.

references.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed
Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
Ask whether SSO, MFA and logging come standard at no extra cost

factors.question: Is the vendor unable to commit (in writing) to deleting our data on request and at contract end?
factors.justification: Data that is never deleted stays exposed forever.
factors.guidance: Look in the DPA / terms for a deletion clause and timeframe.

references.title: Plans include provisions for activities after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
Guidelines for Media Sanitization

factors.question: If this software failed or became unavailable, would that be Catastrophic, Unacceptable, or Acceptable?
factors.justification: Business-continuity view of impact. Carried over from the original template.
factors.guidance: Catastrophic = core operations stop. Unacceptable = major disruption with workarounds. Acceptable = easy fallback.

references.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

factors.question: Does the software support critical teams or business processes (e.g., finance/payments, executive leadership, core operations)?
factors.justification: Critical processes magnify any incident. Weighted 3 (max) by design.
factors.guidance: Edit the examples in this question to match your critical functions.

references.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

factors.question: What is the most sensitive information the software will access?
factors.justification: Standard data-classification ladder: harm grows with sensitivity.
factors.guidance: Sensitive = PII, financial, health, credentials, source code with secrets. Pick the highest that applies.

references.title: Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems
Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

factors.question: If that information were exposed, would it cause direct harm to the people it describes?
factors.justification: Separates embarrassing exposures from ones that hurt real people (identity theft, safety, financial loss).

references.title: PII confidentiality impact levels

factors.question: How widely will this be deployed?
factors.justification: Blast radius: more users means more data and more ways in.

references.title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded

factors.question: What is the highest level of access it gets to our other systems?
factors.justification: Write/admin access means a compromised vendor can change our systems, not just read them.
factors.guidance: Look at the OAuth scopes / API permissions requested.

references.title: Access permissions incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties

factors.question: Will it process data about minors or other vulnerable people?
factors.justification: Higher legal duty of care (e.g., COPPA, GDPR Recital 38) and higher harm if exposed.

references.title: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact are identified and documented
PII confidentiality impact levels
Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule

factors.question: Does the vendor's AI produce or enable explicit, violent, deceptive, or degrading content, or lack enforceable safeguards against such outputs?
factors.justification: Values check. Adds +0.5 to the preference multiplier, so one 'Yes' raises the whole score by 50%. Multiplier rather than points because values concerns should scale the risk, not sit beside it. NIST AI 600-1 names these as generative-AI risks, but there's no NIST guidance on how much they should count against a vendor. Weighing them is an organizational values choice.
factors.guidance: Answer for the vendor's AI, including the parent company's models if they power this product.

references.title: Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content
Obscene, Degrading, and/or Abusive Content

factors.question: Does the vendor use personal data for AI training without meaningful consent, or lack documented protections for vulnerable populations (children, people in crisis)?
factors.justification: Values check (+0.5x). Related NIST guidance exists (AI 600-1 Data Privacy, AI RMF MAP 5.1), but how heavily to weigh it is an organizational values choice.

references.title: Data Privacy
Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact are identified and documented

factors.factor: Training on our data / vendor access
factors.question: Does the vendor train or improve its AI models on our data without an enforceable opt-out, or keep the ability to access, review, or monitor our inputs and outputs?
factors.justification: Values check (+0.5x). Covers the stewardship of data entrusted to us. Contract terms are covered by GV.SC-05, but treating vendor training or monitoring as a values concern that scales the whole score is an organization preference.
factors.guidance: Check the signed DPA, not marketing pages.

references.title: Data Privacy
Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are integrated into contracts

factors.question: Do we have a signed DPA / contract that prohibits training on our data and requires deletion at contract end?
factors.justification: Contract terms make vendor promises enforceable. Cuts final score by 10%.
factors.guidance: Answer Yes only if signed, not just offered.

references.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are integrated into contracts

factors.question: Is a zero-data-retention or privacy mode enforced by an admin for all our users (users cannot turn it off)?
factors.justification: Removes most training and retention exposure. Cuts final score by 10%.

references.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are integrated into contracts
The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

factors.question: Will access be through SSO with automated provisioning/deprovisioning (SCIM), limited to named users?
factors.justification: Shrinks account-takeover and orphaned-account risk. Cuts final score by 5%.

references.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed
Access permissions incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties

factors.question: Is sensitive data blocked from the tool by a technical control (DLP, CASB policy, scoped permissions)?
factors.justification: Enforced limits beat policy-only limits. Cuts final score by 10%.
factors.guidance: A written 'please don't paste PII' policy does not count.

references.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

factors.question: Is approval limited to a time-boxed pilot with a scheduled re-review?
factors.justification: Caps exposure while evidence is gathered. Cuts final score by 5%.

references.title: Supplier risks are understood, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
